phenomena.claim: Geometric gravity at tested scales: solar-system weak-field GR confirmed to ~1e-5 (Shapiro-delay PPN gamma - 1 = (2.1 +/- 2.3)e-5)

phenomena.claim: Gravitational waves exist and were directly detected: prediction 1916, first direct detection 2015 (GW150914, binary black hole merger; waveform matches GR inspiral-merger-ringdown)

phenomena.claim: Gravitational waves propagate at c to ~1e-15 (-3e-15 < (v_gw - c)/c < +7e-16 from the GW170817/GRB 170817A 1.7 s delay), and the polarization content is consistent with GR's two transverse-traceless tensor modes
phenomena.source: speed: LIGO/Virgo/Fermi-GBM/INTEGRAL, ApJ Lett. 848, L13 (2017), arXiv:1710.05834 — bound verified at source 2026-09-23; polarizations: GW170814, PRL 119, 141101 (2017), arXiv:1709.09660 (first tensor-vs-vector/scalar network test) and Tests of GR with GW170817, PRL 123, 011102 (2019), arXiv:1811.00364 (polarization content in agreement with GR) — abstracts verified 2026-09-23; archive: origin/v4:RAI_STRUCTURAL_THEORY_SEARCH.md Answer 1 'exactly two TT polarizations at c to 1e-15'

formalism.claim: Lovelock uniqueness: in 4D, the only symmetric divergence-free rank-2 tensors built from the metric and its first two derivatives are the metric and Einstein tensors, so Einstein-Hilbert + Lambda is the unique second-order metric-only diffeo-invariant dynamics
formalism.source: Lovelock, J. Math. Phys. 12, 498 (1971) — 4D uniqueness statement confirmed at abstract 2026-09-23; archive: origin/v4:RAI_STRUCTURAL_THEORY_SEARCH.md Answer 1 'unique by Lovelock given 4D + second-order + metric-only + diffeo invariance'
formalism.caveat: uniqueness is conditional on all four hypotheses; higher dimensions and higher-derivative/nonlocal actions evade it

symmetries.claim: Diffeomorphism invariance is a gauge redundancy whose Ward identity enforces covariant conservation nabla_mu T^munu = 0 — a symmetry constraint that does NOT by itself select the gravitational action (Einstein-Hilbert, R^2, f(R), Lovelock, and nonlocal curvature actions all satisfy it)

symmetries.caveat: the non-selection statement is community-standard; its use as a no-go against the in-house program is the separate PROGRAM-RESULT entry in known_disconnects

symmetries.claim: The weak equivalence principle (universality of free fall) holds to ~1e-15: Eotvos parameter eta(Ti,Pt) = [-1.5 +/- 2.3(stat) +/- 1.5(syst)]e-15

symmetries.caveat: tests the composition-independence of free fall for the flown mass pair; not a test of the strong equivalence principle
